questions.stem: In Topic 4, select all characteristics belonging to Skeletal Muscle histology: (Select all that apply)
options: B) Multinucleated syncytium with peripheral nuclei
C) Cross-striated A and I bands
E) Intercalated discs with gap junctions
answers: A) Voluntary neural control
B) Multinucleated syncytium with peripheral nuclei
C) Cross-striated A and I bands
D) Subject to rapid fatigue
questions.explanation: Skeletal muscle is voluntary, syncytial, striated, and fatigable.

questions.stem: In Topic 4, select all features distinguishing Cardiac Muscle from Skeletal Muscle: (Select all that apply)
options: B) Branched cardiocytes with central nuclei
C) Intercalated discs providing electrical coupling
answers: A) Involuntary autonomic innervation
B) Branched cardiocytes with central nuclei
C) Intercalated discs providing electrical coupling
D) Resistance to fatigue
questions.explanation: Cardiac muscle is involuntary, branched, fatigue-resistant, and connected by intercalated discs.

questions.stem: In Topic 4, select all connective tissue sheaths organizing skeletal muscle blocks: (Select all that apply)
answers: A) Endomysium (enclosing single muscle fiber)
B) Perimysium (enclosing muscle fascicle bundle)
C) Epimysium (enclosing whole muscle belly)

questions.stem: In Topic 4, select all characteristics of Red Muscle Fibers (Slow Oxidative): (Select all that apply)
options: A) High myoglobin content giving red color
B) Abundant mitochondria for aerobic respiration
D) Slow contraction velocity with high fatigue resistance
answers: A) High myoglobin content giving red color
B) Abundant mitochondria for aerobic respiration
C) Rich blood capillary supply
D) Slow contraction velocity with high fatigue resistance
questions.explanation: Red muscle has high myoglobin, mitochondria, capillaries, aerobic respiration, and high fatigue resistance.

questions.stem: In Topic 4, select all characteristics of White Muscle Fibers (Fast Glycolytic): (Select all that apply)
options: A) Low myoglobin and fewer mitochondria
B) High sarcoplasmic reticulum and fast myosin ATPase
C) Primary reliance on anaerobic glycolysis
D) Fast contraction speed with rapid fatigue
answers: A) Low myoglobin and fewer mitochondria
B) High sarcoplasmic reticulum and fast myosin ATPase
C) Primary reliance on anaerobic glycolysis
D) Fast contraction speed with rapid fatigue
questions.explanation: White muscle has low myoglobin, fast ATPase, anaerobic glycolysis, and rapid fatigue.

questions.stem: In Topic 4, select all regulatory and contractile proteins in Sarcomere: (Select all that apply)
options: D) Troponin C, I, T complex
answers: A) Actin thin filaments
B) Myosin thick filaments
C) Tropomyosin regulatory strands
D) Troponin C, I, T complex
questions.explanation: Sarcomere proteins: Actin, Myosin, Tropomyosin, and Troponin.

questions.stem: In Topic 4, select all ultrastructural Sarcomere changes during muscle contraction: (Select all that apply)
options: B) Narrowing or disappearance of H-zone
D) Movement of Z-lines closer together
E) Lengthening of A-band myosin filaments
answers: A) Shortening of I-band
B) Narrowing or disappearance of H-zone
C) Constant length of A-band
D) Movement of Z-lines closer together
questions.explanation: During contraction, I-band and H-zone shorten, Z-lines approximate, while A-band stays constant.

questions.stem: In Topic 4, select all anatomical locations containing Smooth Muscle tissue: (Select all that apply)
options: A) Wall of gastrointestinal stomach and intestine
B) Wall of blood vessels (Arteries & Veins)
C) Wall of urinary bladder and ureters
answers: A) Wall of gastrointestinal stomach and intestine
B) Wall of blood vessels (Arteries & Veins)
C) Wall of urinary bladder and ureters
D) Wall of respiratory bronchioles
questions.explanation: Smooth muscle lines GI tract, blood vessels, urinary bladder, and bronchioles.

questions.stem: In Topic 4, select all features of Single-Unit Smooth Muscle (Visceral Muscle): (Select all that apply)
options: A) Cells electrically linked via gap junctions
C) Muscle sheet contracts as a single unit syncytium
D) Present in walls of stomach, intestine, and uterus
E) Neurogenic independent cell unit activation
answers: A) Cells electrically linked via gap junctions
B) Demonstrates myogenic pacemaker activity
C) Muscle sheet contracts as a single unit syncytium
D) Present in walls of stomach, intestine, and uterus
questions.explanation: Single-unit smooth muscle is myogenic, coupled by gap junctions, and contracts as a syncytium in visceral organs.

questions.stem: In Topic 4, select all cell junctions present inside Cardiac Intercalated Discs: (Select all that apply)
options: D) Tight Junctions (blocking all ionic flow)
answers: A) Fascia Adherens (anchoring actin filaments)
B) Macula Adherens / Desmosomes (mechanical anchoring)
C) Gap Junctions (longitudinal impulse transmission)
questions.explanation: Intercalated discs contain Fascia Adherens, Desmosomes, and Gap Junctions.
